researchProtocol.lookback: Last 30–60 days for material events, with most recent available issuer results and explicitly dated future releases.
researchProtocol.evidenceClass: Original filings/IR and official releases preferred. Reuters/industry reporters secondary. Source gaps flagged explicitly. None of this is a contemporaneous executable quote or verified broker account.
researchProtocol.readiness: News != sufficient valuation; issuer cash, guidance, price, debt, consensus, event timing and broker holdings require separate proof.
researchProtocol.restrictions: No changes to original holdings, cost, conviction scores, watchlist categories, allocation, trade status or canonical Bluebelly Dossier. No orders or new scheduled tasks.
researchProtocol.apiHealth: FMP stock-news endpoint rejected, Alpha Vantage news rate-limited, Finnhub newsroom denied 403. Public issuer/filings and dated news searched independently. Exhaustive real-time newswire retrieval not claimed.

marketContext.asOf: 29 Oct US close / 30 Oct pre-US-open Asia
themes: AI buyer capex vs supplier cash collection
sticky September PCE vs falling Treasuries
oil/LNG product spread versus real cargoes

holdings.headline: Q3 earnings are scheduled; do not treat estimates as reported results.
holdings.facts: ExxonMobil's investor relations calendar schedules its Q3 2026 financial results for 30 October US morning, after the 12:15 MYT research cutoff. Brent above $110 in some October contract-month readings is supportive of crude realisations, but refining margins, chemical margins, upstream production and taxes determine consolidated earnings. No verified Q3 result is admitted here.
holdings.impact: The earnings test can materially change the valuation of the existing XOM position. The investor needs Q3 operating cash, organic capex, dividend/buyback coverage, Guyana and Permian volume, realised crude/gas prices and refining spreads before upgrading the hold.
holdings.countercase: Strong integrated diversification and long-cycle low-cost barrels could stabilise cash generation even if the oil-risk premium fades. Conversely a high crude quote can coexist with weak products and heavy capex.
holdings.nextProof: Obtain 30 October issuer release and 10-Q after publication; compare consolidated CFO minus cash capex, segment EPS, dividend+buyback and realised benchmark price with the prior two quarters.

holdings.headline: Long charters improve revenue visibility, but signed terms and build cash still matter.
holdings.facts: On 7 October the company disclosed letters of award for five newbuild LNG carriers intended for 20-year charters starting in 2030; a separate 9 October announcement described a new 18,700-cbm LNG carrier and 10-year charter scheduled from 2028. These are two distinct vessels/contract families. October press also cited an extension of a possible Yinson privatisation proposal, not a completed acquisition.
holdings.impact: Contracted shipping backlog is positive for long-run earning visibility and offsets some volatile spot LNG-market exposure, but the short-term share-price call depends on shipbuilding capex, debt/lease structure and current operating tanker/vessel earnings. Do not count non-final LOAs as already earning cash.
holdings.countercase: Long-tenor charters can finance newbuilds through contracted customer payments; the countercase is capital tie-up, delivery slippage and lower long-term charter returns after shipyard costs.
holdings.nextProof: Verify final charter party signatures and counterparties, purchase/construction costs, charter rates or contracted margin, financing structure, delivery schedule and FY26 earnings excluding vessel-disposal gains.

holdings.headline: FY2026 profits improved; test how much is repeatable at today’s realised oil prices.
holdings.facts: Hibiscus's investor-relations material and recent FY2026 reports cite profit around RM361 million, up sharply year on year, with a 10-sen annual dividend. The latest 29 October AGM updates are governance communications rather than a new Q3 earnings event. Production volumes, depreciation, depletion and field-level cash costs were not completely reconciled in this sweep.
holdings.impact: The holding is fundamentally different from refiners or tanker operators: oil and gas selling prices matter, but sustaining mature-field production and cash after development spending matters more. Higher Brent is not proof the production profile or net free cash flow improved.
holdings.countercase: Existing producing fields may generate cash at attractive realised prices and support distributions. The downside is declining output, well interventions, licensing/tax exposure and rising restoration commitments.
holdings.nextProof: Read latest September-quarter or AGM presentation: FY26 actual production by basin, realised gas/oil prices, lifting cost/boe, capex, debt, reserves and payout affordability.

holdings.headline: A large Selangor industrial-park partnership is strategic acreage, not proven contracted AI cash.
holdings.facts: YTL Power, SD Guthrie and Bumi Assets announced a partnership around approximately 1,623 acres in Bukit Kerayong, Selangor. The planned interest split is 35% YTL Power, 30% SD Guthrie and 35% Bumi Assets, with land valued near RM934 million in the venture. The company has also announced Siemens gas-turbine-related power equipment initiatives. These arrangements are not equivalent to signed, financed data-centre tenants or a new consolidated earnings contribution.
holdings.impact: The company has credible exposure to Malaysian power and industrial development, but significant common-stock and linked-warrant concentration means new project ambitions increase sensitivity to financing, execution and electricity tariff economics. Distinguish property JV equity and utility operating earnings.
holdings.countercase: Land access and power availability may become scarce strategic assets and attract credible operators. Alternatively construction cost, dilution, project debt and tenants’ willingness to pay could compress equity returns.
holdings.nextProof: Obtain JV filings, stage-specific capital commitments, tenant offtake, interconnection cost recovery, regulated earnings and current Bursa position value before considering additional capital.

holdings.headline: Your YTL-linked warrant cannot be underwritten as an ordinary share.
holdings.facts: PowerStack's broker-ledger alias 6742UW remains unresolved: it is not safely mapped to a current Bursa structured-warrant ISIN, issuer or term sheet. Web results show several distinct YTLPOWR structured call warrants with different strikes, conversion ratios and 2027 expiries, plus the company's separate 2025–28 own-issued warrant; none can safely be treated as 6742UW without confirmation. A stock rise need not rescue an out-of-money, time-decaying warrant.
holdings.impact: Capital at risk can be 100% of premium with high sensitivity to underlying price, remaining life, implied volatility, exercise terms and market-maker quotes. This warrants verification ahead of all other portfolio news. Do not claim the company’s 2028 ordinary-share-exercisable warrant is the same as an unrelated 2027 structured call.
holdings.countercase: A correctly identified warrant may offer positive leveraged upside if the share moves enough before expiry. Liquidity, spread widening and accelerated time decay can instead erase the position despite a sound company thesis.
holdings.nextProof: Match the exact broker contract description, Bursa short name and ISIN, issuer, call/put, exercise price, conversion ratio, adjusted underlying, expiry, issue/market price, bid/ask and held units. Then compute cash-settlement payoff and breakeven.

holdings.headline: GTA VI launch is approaching; bookings are not the same as cash collected today.
holdings.facts: Take-Two's first-quarter fiscal 2027 release showed approximately $1.39 billion in net bookings and full-year bookings guidance of $8.0–8.2 billion. The last issuer-verified public launch target used in this audit is 19 November 2026 for Grand Theft Auto VI. Do not assert that it has shipped or estimate full game unit sales before launch.
holdings.impact: The approaching major product cycle can strengthen the long-run content economics, but the stock's discounted future cash may already anticipate strong day-one sales. Marketing, development expenditure, platform take rates, online engagement and execution/delay risk can all shift the risk/reward. Next reported results matter more than social pre-order rumours.
holdings.countercase: A record franchise launch and durable online spending could justify very high initial expectations. Another scheduling change, pricing resistance or poor monetisation could create outsized disappointment.
holdings.nextProof: Check latest official Rockstar/Take-Two launch confirmation, fiscal Q2 actual bookings/adjusted operating income, remaining software costs, preorder disclosure and no-delayed-launch warnings.

holdings.headline: The SpaceX possibility adds event risk to an operating-margin and free-cash-flow question.
holdings.facts: Tesla's Q3 SEC 10-Q reported revenue about $28.05 billion and GAAP operating income about $0.718 billion; operating margin was roughly 2.6%, down sharply year on year. Nine-month cash flow from operations was $14.897 billion against $13.014 billion cash property/equipment spending, yielding simple FCF about $1.883 billion, well below the previous year's comparable simple FCF. Tesla invested roughly $2.002 billion in SpaceX equity separately from cash capex; it also disclosed SpaceX commercial receivables and deferred revenue. Both boards have explored a possible combination through special committees, but no signed merger ratio or closing is established.
holdings.impact: The company has substantial cash plus securities, but operating profitability and capex payback drive intrinsic returns. Its SpaceX financing and commercial linkages must be treated as disclosed exposures, not proven misconduct or an executed merger. Security pricing at or near $400 needs a separate valuation sensitivity.
holdings.countercase: Tesla's energy deployments, AI/robotics options and substantial liquidity may support long-duration returns. However, the standalone car margin squeeze, launch spending and potential related-party complexity can hurt shareholders even in a strong tech market.
holdings.nextProof: Reconcile Q3/YTD margins, CFO versus cash capex and SpaceX settlement; obtain definitive merger legal terms if announced; compare current price with forward earnings/FCF and realistic energy/vehicle unit economics.

holdings.headline: Weak contract execution makes this an operating-repair story, not merely an oil-price bet.
holdings.facts: Dayang reported second-quarter 2026 revenue approximately RM161.2 million, compared with RM267.3 million one year earlier; profit attributable to owners fell to approximately RM32.8 million from RM76.6 million. The source is a completed quarterly earnings filing, not a forecast. Recent October ownership or corporate announcements do not by themselves demonstrate restoration of vessel activity, offshore maintenance utilisation or margin.
holdings.impact: For this existing losing position, a higher Brent future improves customer incentive to spend only after project budgets, backlog conversions and invoice collections follow through. With the profit base markedly lower, do not average down purely on crude prices or an unchanged historical share score.
holdings.countercase: A temporary contract lull could reverse as Malaysia offshore work orders and customer spending rise; alternatively lower utilisation, wage/vessel cost and working-capital pressure may persist for several quarters.
holdings.nextProof: Obtain next Bursa quarterly results and latest order-book utilisation, vessel days, receivables, cash/debt, new contract awards and subcontractor costs; reassess whether cash would be better deployed elsewhere.

watchlist.headline: HBM demand is real; capex and cash conversion decide the share-price upside.
watchlist.facts: Micron's latest available fiscal Q4 / FY2026 official filing reported exceptional memory revenue growth tied to HBM and broader DRAM/NAND pricing. Its report reflects the completed September period, not a new October earnings surprise. A tight memory cycle can lift margins sharply while wafer-fab and HBM advanced-packaging spending rises in parallel.
watchlist.impact: Higher HBM mix supports structural earnings growth but large orders and chip shortages can overstate sustainable cycle margins. Check FCF after plant capex, customer prepayments, 2027 supply commitments and price versus earnings on current share count.
watchlist.countercase: AI customers may secure long-duration purchases, limiting the old commodity cycle. Faster Chinese supply and later capacity additions could also compress HBM/DRAM margins.
watchlist.nextProof: Track next quarter HBM4 yields and contracted volume, gross margin outlook, CFO minus capex, inventory and days of supply; refresh same-date price and valuation.

watchlist.headline: Raised LNG outlook rests on cargo delivery and liquefaction economics.
watchlist.facts: Cheniere's 29 October Q3 report raised its projected 2026 adjusted EBITDA range to about $8.75–9.25 billion; reported roughly 188 LNG export cargoes during Q3, with revenue about $6.1 billion. Expansion trains and long-term sales contracts offer different exposure from spot crude. The raised outlook is guidance rather than realised final-year FCF.
watchlist.impact: The stronger earnings outlook supports contractual LNG cash generation in an energy-security regime, but construction spending, variable feedgas costs, terminal reliability and future debt maturities still determine common-equity cash returns.
watchlist.countercase: Long-duration take-or-pay style contracts can make cash more resilient than spot commodity prices; war premiums may reverse and reduce margin on opportunistic cargoes.
watchlist.nextProof: Compare official Q3 release CFO/capex, contracted vs merchant volumes, trains commissioning schedule, debt cash interest and 2027 dividend/share-repurchase capacity.

watchlist.headline: 1.6T optical cables address an AI bottleneck; product claims are not order receipts.
watchlist.facts: Credo introduced its ZeroFlap 1.6T active-light-cable system with short-reach, 50-metre row-scale ambitions and said deliveries would ramp later. Related October announcements described high-speed interconnect collaboration with AMD. Technical specifications and launch plans cannot be equated with shipped paid datacentre units.
watchlist.impact: High-performance connectivity can become a profitable picks-and-shovels supplier as GPU clusters expand, but product-development costs, a concentrated customer base, competitor qualifications and price compression could shrink the expected benefit.
watchlist.countercase: A defensible architecture and low failure rate could win repeat platform designs; faster low-cost alternatives or stronger incumbent networking vendors could displace it.
watchlist.nextProof: Verify design wins converted into GAAP sales, 1.6T shipments, hyperscaler share, gross margin, customer concentration and next quarterly gross-profit-to-cash conversion.

watchlist.headline: Atome changes Grab from marketplace turnaround into consumer-credit underwriting.
watchlist.facts: Grab announced a proposed approximately $1.49 billion acquisition of 60% of Atome Financial, with a performance-linked later acquisition of the remaining interest. Closing is expected in 2027, not completed. The company also discussed an October Sarawak AI partnership, but that is not a proven near-term consolidated profit driver.
watchlist.impact: Delivery/mobility marketplace improvements and financial-services growth should be measured separately. New consumer lending introduces loan-loss provisioning, balance-sheet funding, regulatory capital, delinquency vintage and collection risks that can consume apparent adjusted EBITDA improvements.
watchlist.countercase: Atome distribution could expand high-return finance services if underwriting stays disciplined; a recession or looser lending standards could consume the marketplace cash cushion.
watchlist.nextProof: Obtain Atome credit-vintage delinquency, net charge-offs, funding liabilities, acquisition earn-out and actual segment FCF. Match current GRAB share price and EV to credible 2028 EBITDA/FCF sensitivity.

watchlist.headline: Fuel awards extend a profitable operating franchise beyond reactor concepts.
watchlist.facts: BWX Technologies announced a multi-year TRISO fuel-production agreement with Antares on 27 October, alongside earlier October BANR microreactor developments. Nuclear fuel, naval propulsion and government supply are nearer-term cash-generative franchises than many pre-revenue SMR developers, but an announcement does not identify realised cash or exact award economics.
watchlist.impact: Reinforces diversified defence/nuclear backlog growth; margin and free cash flow depend on capacity upgrades, project timing, and whether commercial pilot commitments become repeat orders. A strong business can still be an expensive stock.
watchlist.countercase: Government programmes and fuel certification provide long barriers to entry. Risks include budget timing, cost overruns, license delays and aggressive valuation.
watchlist.nextProof: Reconcile latest issuer funded backlog vs unfunded awards, Q3/FY guidance, adjusted-to-GAAP earnings bridge, annual capex, TRISO deliveries and valuation after the next print.

watchlist.headline: Enterprise AI systems expand the sales pitch, not yet the proof of cash margin.
watchlist.facts: Dell and NVIDIA unveiled new AI Factory capabilities on 21 October, referencing thousands of customer deployments and future product availability into 2027. The disclosure supports enterprise demand but mixes installed customers, future systems and marketing language; hardware booked backlog is not automatically high-margin recognised revenue.
watchlist.impact: Server sales can rise sharply while GPUs, memory and customer financing absorb working capital and margins. Distinguish Dell's infrastructure growth, enterprise storage and client PC business from the 2027 product roadmap.
watchlist.countercase: Scaled supply chains and services attach may produce recurring returns; component shortages, customer concentration and heavy integration costs can keep net FCF low.
watchlist.nextProof: Check latest ISG AI-server shipped revenues and backlog, gross margin by segment, receivable days, inventory financing, cloud-service attach rate and next Dell quarter.

watchlist.headline: Google's nuclear PPA is credible demand but new megawatts arrive on a schedule.
watchlist.facts: Constellation and Google announced a long-duration agreement for an estimated 890 MW of additional output from upgrades at 11 nuclear plants, complementing an earlier Amazon-linked nuclear power agreement. Existing generation and contract counterparties make this different from speculative greenfield SMRs. Additional MW are projected, not already dispatched today.
watchlist.impact: Long-term contracted power may support cash and valuable transmission-ready supply, yet repowering capex, outage risk, nuclear fuel, regulatory permission and project start dates determine returns. Watch PPA financial terms rather than assume data-centre power is universally priced at a premium.
watchlist.countercase: High-quality counterparties can de-risk incremental MW. Wholesale-market volatility and lower-price repricing could still weaken margins once hedges roll.
watchlist.nextProof: Obtain contracted output start dates, customer credit support, incremental cost per MW, nuclear fleet availability, hedged electricity prices and net debt maturities.

watchlist.headline: The seed separation changes the instrument and invalidates pre-spin comparisons.
watchlist.facts: Corteva's October separation created Vylor for seed operations, leaving legacy Corteva focused on crop protection. The process includes share/ownership allocation mechanics in SEC disclosure. Historical CTVA close prices, combined EPS and revenue before separation cannot be compared to post-spin security prices without adjustments.
watchlist.impact: PowerStack's historical 8.7 score and ag-science rationale must be read in light of a materially different business. New investment underwriting should begin with standalone pro-forma cash, debt, specialty chemical margins and crop-cycle demand; do not use unadjusted old chart levels as technical triggers.
watchlist.countercase: The remaining company may offer clearer capital returns and focused investment; the old seed franchise may have held the more defensive IP growth, reducing standalone quality.
watchlist.nextProof: Confirm distribution ratio/ex-date and CTVA/Vylor identifiers; obtain first pro-forma balance sheets, continuing-operation CFO/capex, pesticide volume trends and post-spin adjusted valuation.

watchlist.headline: Copper's strategic demand does not erase Grasberg mine execution risk.
watchlist.facts: Freeport's investor relations indicates third-quarter results were released on 27 October. Copper demand from power grids and data centres remains a structural support, but Indonesia's Grasberg operations and shipment timing can overwhelm a benchmark copper-price rally in any single quarter. Specific Q3 tonnes, unit cash costs and capex figures were not independently extracted in this sweep.
watchlist.impact: Underwrite recovery of mined/sold volume and attributable FCF, not a generic AI copper narrative. Project restart schedules and safety/legal costs may change both near-term cash and future reserves.
watchlist.countercase: Long-lived low-cost copper assets can benefit from electrification and constrained global supply. Production disruptions and high-grade transitions may offset copper price gains.
watchlist.nextProof: Open issuer Q3 presentation and verify Grasberg output/recovery plan, concentrate inventories, attributable sales, unit net cash cost/lb, cash capex and 2027 production guide.

watchlist.headline: Potash volumes and nitrogen feedstock dynamics can diverge.
watchlist.facts: Nutrien issued October operational commentary on its Trinidad nitrogen operation; its completed second-quarter report showed strong potash sales volumes but a mixed nitrogen cycle. A November quarterly print remains an upcoming catalyst at this audit cutoff. Grain/fertiliser prices, farmer economics, potash contract pricing and feedgas shocks differ by product.
watchlist.impact: The agriculture sleeve can diversify AI duration exposure, but feedgas-cost shocks, farmer affordability and capital-intensity can reduce FCF despite strong tonnage. Compare current selling prices with the prior quarter rather than assume every fertiliser producer wins from scarcity.
watchlist.countercase: Supply disruption can sustain higher potash and nitrogen pricing; crop income stress can ultimately suppress demand and produce inventory accumulation.
watchlist.nextProof: Verify Q3 official release timing, Trinidad outage duration, potash realised price and tonnes, nitrogen cost margins, North America retail earnings, net debt and FCF.

watchlist.headline: The $63bn Anthropic plan is a demand and counterparty-credit question.
watchlist.facts: Broadcom and financing partners announced an approximately $63 billion structured financing arrangement for Anthropic-related AI hardware infrastructure, involving first-lien bank capital, Blackstone second-lien exposure and Broadcom residual-value support. Proposed commitments, closing draws, delivery and recognised chip revenue are different states.
watchlist.impact: The proposed arrangement illustrates substantial expected custom-compute demand, but support for the residual value of accelerators can transfer technology obsolescence and credit risk back to suppliers. The investor should stress-test how much of 'AI backlog' is truly cash-funded.
watchlist.countercase: Access to committed debt and reliable end-customer demand may accelerate high-margin hardware revenue; if utilisation or AI pricing disappoints, collateral values and borrower ability to refinance become central.
watchlist.nextProof: Read definitive SPV agreements and Broadcom filings for maximum residual guarantees, collateral treatment, cash draw timetable, customer take-or-pay and GAAP revenue recognition.

watchlist.headline: Q3 call lies ahead of the Asia research cutoff.
watchlist.facts: Cameco scheduled its third-quarter 2026 release and conference call for 30 October North American time. Uranium term contracting, production/lb sales, inventory and Westinghouse earnings are more decision-useful than a headline uranium spot quote. As of this noon-Malaysia cutoff, the Q3 results are not included as realised facts.
watchlist.impact: Fuel contracting with utilities can smooth some volatility, but guidance changes and Westinghouse's service/capital commitments matter materially. Avoid buying solely because nuclear power is linked to AI demand.
watchlist.countercase: Supply discipline and long-term utility needs are constructive; term pricing already embedded in stock multiples and execution underdelivery could disappoint.
watchlist.nextProof: Read newly published issuer Q3 after release: realised price per pound, contracted volumes, production, Westinghouse contribution, CFO/capex and 2027 guidance.

watchlist.headline: Strong first-half nitrogen returns are not the same as a clean recurring run rate.
watchlist.facts: CF Industries' latest first-half 2026 report showed $1.34 billion net earnings and $2.18 billion adjusted EBITDA, including an approximately $170 million litigation settlement gain. Product prices rose amid supply disruption and Iran-related scarcity while aggregate volumes declined, including Yazoo City lost availability. The company announced its next earnings call for 5 November; the actual Q3 announcement is expected immediately before that, not already verified.
watchlist.impact: This is an attractive non-AI cash engine only if net fertiliser-gas spreads and sales volumes persist after the supply disruption. Shareholder FCF must exclude one-offs and allow for Blue Point low-carbon ammonia capital requirements.
watchlist.countercase: Scarcity and North American cost advantage can sustain margins; demand elasticity and new global capacity could make current earnings peak-cyclical.
watchlist.nextProof: Verify Q3 normalised cash earnings, nitrogen-gas unit spreads, volume recovery, Yazoo City restart, committed Blue Point cash calls, dividend and buybacks; check current CF stock valuation.

watchlist.headline: Alibaba's accelerating cloud economics come with new equity issuance.
watchlist.facts: Alibaba's August quarter results showed AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue near $7.1 billion, up 45% year-on-year, with cloud adjusted EBITA up about 133%. The issuer also disclosed completion of an HK$80 billion new-share placing in late August. That is operational momentum alongside potential shareholder dilution and funding needs; no later October official quarter was found in the primary issuer listing at this cutoff.
watchlist.impact: China AI adoption can lift Alibaba cloud margins and economies of scale, but incremental compute spend, price competition, regulatory risk and equity dilution must be reflected in per-share returns. Commerce cash remains an important source of AI funding.
watchlist.countercase: An integrated China cloud/commerce franchise may sustain AI monetisation despite chip restrictions. Domestic competition, AI inference price pressure and geopolitics may absorb these gains.
watchlist.nextProof: Review actual cloud EBITA/capex/FCF, share count after placing, Qwen paid usage and buybacks; compare HK versus US listing and current exchange/FX quote.

watchlist.headline: Record backlog and strong cash distinguish GEV from pre-funded AI projects.
watchlist.facts: GE Vernova's 28 October third-quarter report disclosed approximately $197 billion in backlog, $12.6 billion quarterly revenue, $6.1 billion operating cash flow and $5.4 billion free cash flow, as well as higher full-year guidance. It separately announced an agreement to acquire Trench for roughly $9 billion, subject to closing conditions. Heavy customer deposits and turbine slot reservations require careful cash-quality analysis.
watchlist.impact: GEV provides actual gas turbines, grid and electrification bottlenecks. Its order book and cash collections support a real operating thesis, but not automatically current valuation or completion of the acquisition.
watchlist.countercase: Multi-year equipment supply and power shortages support pricing and margins; large backlog can contain cancellation clauses, delivery risk and advance-payment timing that reverse later.
watchlist.nextProof: Reconcile backlog additions to deposits and revenue, cash conversion excluding advances, capex, after-tax acquisition returns, turbine slot utilisation and share valuation.

watchlist.headline: Preferred redemption and coming earnings merit more scrutiny than generic nuclear optimism.
watchlist.facts: Vistra's late-October issuer announcements include an October 15 redemption of outstanding 8% Series A preferred shares and an October 29 common/preferred dividend declaration. Q3 earnings are scheduled for 6 November. These are verifiable capital-structure and shareholder-return events, not new contracted megawatts or 30 October earnings.
watchlist.impact: Retiring expensive preferred capital can lower future distributions, but only after replacement funding and timing are measured. Existing generating assets and PPAs should be valued on realised power/hedge spreads, fleet outages and net leverage.
watchlist.countercase: Scarce dispatchable power can command long-duration prices; volatile merchant power, environmental liabilities and aggressive AI-utility multiples may erode upside.
watchlist.nextProof: Obtain redemption financing and expense, Nov 6 Q3 CFO/FCF, hedge books, capacity revenue, actual nuclear/gas generation and net debt per MW.

nextSteps: Verify every ticker local listing, earnings release and current quote before repricing security.
Distinguish historic earnings, today-published figures and future earnings.
Preserve Bluebelly/Notion research-only distinction and conflicting provider clocks.
Investigate instrument 6742UW and Rakuten holdings/cash before any trade.
